overview: This Senate resolution condemns the June 1, 2025, attack on a peaceful march in Boulder, Colorado, held by Run for Their Lives, a group calling for the release of hostages taken by Hamas in its October 7, 2023, attack on Israel. The attacker used a makeshift flamethrower and Molotov cocktails, injuring several people, including a Holocaust survivor, and authorities investigated it as terrorism and a federal hate crime. The resolution expresses solidarity with the survivors and their families, praises the Boulder community, and calls for continued vigilance and federal resources to counter rising antisemitism and investigate hate crimes. It affirms that people of all faiths deserve to live free from fear and persecution. The Senate agreed to it by unanimous consent on June 12, 2025.
for: Supporters say the Senate should speak with one voice in condemning a violent antisemitic attack on peaceful marchers and in standing with Jewish communities facing growing threats.
against: Critics say the resolution is symbolic and doesn't itself change any law or provide any of the federal resources it calls for.
